writeup: A candidate eclipsing binary star designated TIC 463349042 has been identified through automated analysis of TESS photometry data. The system shows a primary eclipse with a depth of 10.78 percent occurring every 15.5669 days, while no secondary eclipse was detected. The eclipse signal achieved a detection significance of 524.7 in the box-least-squares search, with pixel-level image analysis confirming a peak signal-to-noise ratio of 54.9 and a centroid offset of 2.0 arcsec from the target location. The candidate does not appear in six major variable-star catalogs, and the machine-learning screening assigned it a score of 0.65, indicating substantial likelihood of being a real target. All data quality checks passed without flagging concerns.
